title: Retail Sales Performance Report: 2023-2024
executive_summary: Total revenue for 2023-2024 was $445,325.09 across 520 cleaned orders, an average order value of $856.39. Revenue grew 10.08% year over year in 2024, building from $36,108.31 in Q1 to a $71,674.99 peak in Q3. East is the strongest region at $130,516.69. Order revenue is highly skewed toward a few large orders, and the top single customer accounts for 6.24% of revenue.

key_findings.statement: Overall performance: total revenue of $445,325.09 was generated from 520 orders, giving an average order value of $856.39.
Regional comparison: East leads with $130,516.69, followed by North ($124,845.75), West ($99,428.16) and South ($90,534.49); East outperforms the weakest region, South, by $39,982.20.
2024 quarterly trend: revenue climbed steadily from $36,108.31 in Q1 to $56,616.79 in Q2 and a peak of $71,674.99 in Q3, before easing slightly to $68,948.71 in Q4; Q3 exceeded Q1 by $35,566.68.
Year-over-year change: revenue increased 10.08%, rising from $211,976.29 in 2023 to $233,348.80 in 2024, an absolute gain of $21,372.51.
High-discount electronics: 22 Electronics orders carried a discount of 20% or more, contributing $50,035.33 in revenue, equal to 11.24% of total revenue from just 4.23% of all orders.

Order revenue distribution is strongly right-skewed: the mean of $856.39 sits well above the median of $313.28, with a large standard deviation of $1,295.74 and values spanning $5.27 to $7,844.02, indicating a minority of very large orders pulls the average up.
Customer concentration is low: 222 unique customers purchased in the period, and the highest-revenue customer spent $27,793.13, representing 6.24% of total revenue.

limitations: The analysis covers revenue only; no cost, margin or returns data were available, so the profitability of the 22 heavily discounted Electronics orders cannot be judged.
Only two years of history exist, and the quarterly trend covers 2024 alone, so seasonal patterns cannot be separated from one-off events.
Order revenue is highly skewed (standard deviation $1,295.74 exceeds the mean of $856.39), so averages are heavily influenced by a small number of large orders.
Customer concentration was measured using only the single top customer; broader concentration (for example the top 5 or 10 customers) was not computed.
The currency of revenue figures is not specified in the source data.
conclusion: 2024 was a growth year, with revenue up 10.08% to $233,348.80 and momentum peaking in Q3 at $71,674.99. Priorities for stakeholders: build on the strong East and North regions, address the lagging South, review the margin impact of deep Electronics discounts, and manage the revenue risk embedded in a small number of very large orders.
